server.encryption: required by both client profile and synthetic Samba share

groups: encrypted SMB3 connection and truthful capabilities
raw SMB provider create/content/metadata/content receipts retain strong guards, metadata and reject external edits without refetch
checks: SMB3 encrypted session succeeds while server and client require transport encryption
Create response immediately contains the exact Finder tag plist and selected user xattrs just published
Content modification succeeds immediately after create without a provider fetch
Metadata-only modification returns the exact new tags and user xattrs
Another content modification succeeds immediately after metadata-only modification without a provider fetch
Each successful operation persists a strong revision matching one of its confirmed own-write receipts while SMB enumeration remains weak
A separate SMB client publishes an external version; the stale provider overwrite reports version_conflict and preserves external bytes

scope: Focused raw SMB provider IPC receipt and continuous-edit proof. Historical ten-group SMB CLI/lifecycle validation is preserved separately in SMB_VALIDATION.json. No real NAS or cloud storage was contacted.
limits: The exact negotiated SMB dialect was not captured; the server accepts only SMB3_00 through SMB3_11.
This validates the Rust provider bridge over encrypted SMB, not macOS native File Provider activation or server power-loss durability.
path_format: Artifact paths are repository-relative; machine-specific prefixes were omitted before initial publication.
